skill: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot
learner_operation: Translate three linear equations into a 3x4 augmented matrix, identify the single independent row, normalize its pivot and eliminate its multiples; select the resulting RREF. At moderate difficulty also express the pivot variable using two free variables.
reasoning_steps: Use a nonzero pivot row, scale its pivot to one, eliminate the other two rows.
For easy select the unique RREF; for moderate translate the surviving equation into the general solution.
response_contract: Five-choice radio: easy matrix RREF; moderate parametric vector solution. Canonical example has no answer field.
difficulty: Easy: rank-one consistent 3x3 systems with small integer proportional rows, often a unit leading coefficient. Moderate adds solving for free variables.
invariants: Three equations and variables; coefficient rank one and augmented rank one.
Exactly one normalized pivot and two zero rows in RREF.
Row operations and intermediate matrices must agree.
Exactly one correct radio option; preserve complete source banks at replay.
permitted_variations: Vary signs and magnitudes of the independent equation, right-hand constant, and nonzero row multipliers.
Vary row order and whether a unit pivot is already present.
Vary answer position and incorrect sign, constant, rank, normalization or pivot mistakes.
Leading nonzero variable can conservatively vary when preceding coefficients are zero, without adding rank or operations; x being first is observed but not essential to rank-one reduction.
Vary which choices survive rank/RREF shape checks: matching rank is mathematical reasoning, but a unique shape must not replace checking row equivalence.

fixed_features.justification: Knowledge point and tutorial 3950 explicitly concern one-pivot systems; adding rank or inconsistency would change the family.
Every supplied question uses this response contract.
